heading: 9.3 Takaful / Insurance Coverage Instructions Introduction
content:
For Hypothecated / Pledged Stock / Fixed Assets (SE/ME / Commercial /
Corporate) All movables & immovable hypothecated / pledged / leased / mortgaged assets must be fully
insured (i.e. coverage value not less than outstanding finance plus approved margin or operative
limit whichever is higher) against all risks pertinent to the assets keeping in view area / storage
conditions at customer's premises and 3rd party godowns during complete tenor of outstanding
liabilities through Takaful / Insurance policies issued by companies on Banks approved list.

Being an Islamic Bank it is ESSENTIAL to obtain TAKAFUL Policy, however, in the absence of
Islamic Insurance alternatives in the country / area of operation, the Bank may obtain conventional
form of Insurance on the basis of genuine need / extreme necessity (any deviation to be accorded as
prescribed in Annexure FM: 9.17)

Details of assets to be insured are mentioned below:

*   Movable hypothecated stocks
*   Movable pledged stocks
*   Leased assets / Diminishing Musharakah assets
*   Movable hypothecated / (plant & machinery)
*   Mortgage (building / structure / fittings)

For financing up to Rs 2 million in case of both Small Enterprise and Medium Enterprise, the
finance approving authority may waive the condition to obtain Takaful/Insurance Cover of
hypothecated stock/other securities, keeping in view the creditworthiness of the customers, his/
her past experience and financial strength.

Takaful / Insurance Coverage against financing facilities extended by Consumer Banking Group to
be applicable as per instructions mentioned under different approved Product Program Manuals.

heading: 9.3.2 Risk Coverage
content:
Takaful / Insurance should be arranged for stock / movable & immovable assets including in transit
(where applicable) to cover transportation by sea vessel (marine insurance as mandatory), Road and
Air.

Following ALL RISKS should be covered at customers cost and Bank to be beneficiary of this
Takaful / Insurance policy:

1.  Fire
2.  Riot & Strike Damage (RSD)
3.  Malicious Damage
4.  Burglary / Theft (for residential assets excluding buildings).
5.  Earthquake
6.  Atmospheric Disturbance
7.  Impact Damage
8.  Aircraft Damage
9.  Electrical Clause
10. Explosion
11. Terrorism

A chart as per Annexure FM: 9.16 is provided as guidance to identify minimum risk coverage.
Business Units / Branches should assess the pertinent risk(s) on a case-to-case basis in relation to
nature of assets, storage condition, and atmospheric condition of the area etc where these assets are
held as security.

EXCEPTIONS / WAIVERS may be extended for SPECIFIC RISK COVERAGE based on Joint /
Individual Insurance Policy, location and strong footing of customer (please refer to Annexure FM:
9.17).

heading: 9.3.3 Basic Risk Coverage Requirements
content:
Appended below are basic risk coverage requirements provided as a guidance, nevertheless,
business unit and CAD to ensure all requirements under Para(s) 9.3.4, 9.3.5, 9.3.6 & 9.3.19 are
complied in all aspects (where applicable):

*   Cover Note to be acceptable for a period of up to 30 days following validity / Expiry of
    Insurance/Takaful Policy subject to approval by Regional Corporate Head/Head-SME &
    Commercial .Approval for beyond 30 days and up-to 60 days in the presence of Cover Note will
    be given by Group Head- Business.
*   Assignment of Takaful / Insurance policy in Bank's favor is appearing as follows:
    *   Hypothecated Assets: MBL as “Mortgagor" / Loss Payee
    *   Ijarah/Leased Assets: MBL as “Owner and Lessor” & Customer as “User and Lessee” OR
        MBL as “insured on account of customer”
    *   Mortgage (land & building): MBL as “Mortgagee” and customer as “Mortgagor”
*   Comprehensive Takaful / Insurance policy covering Risks as per finance approval or in case
    approval is silent all risks as stated in Para# 9.3.2 MUST be covered except where approval of
    competent authority obtained as per Annexure FM: 9.17.
*   Description of property / leased assets / goods (stocks, plant & machinery, building etc.)
    matches as per credit approval.
*   The location(s) of Assets (i.e. Pledged / Leased / Mortgaged/Hypothecated) mentioned in the
    Takaful/Insurance Policy should match with the location(s) mentioned in the Memorandum of
    Deposit of Title Deeds, Lease / Diminishing Musharakah agreement Stock and Pledge report (to
    mention specific address(es) or anywhere in Pakistan).
*   Assets which are frequently moved from one site to another site or situated in various locations
    (such as pipelines, transmission lines etc) must be insured with jurisdiction clause of insurance
    coverage “various locations / anywhere in Pakistan”.
*   Value of Takaful / Insurance is adequate to cover MBL's exposure (i.e. outstanding) /operative
    limit with security margin.
*   Adhesive stamps of required value are affixed on the face of original insurance policy.
*   Business Unit & CAD to ensure Any restrictive clause (the clauses which comes specifically
    under the specific heading of restrictive clauses) or specific storage conditions (particularly for
    commodity financing) mentioned in Takaful / Insurance policy are complied to avoid any
    dispute in the event of any claim or alternatively unachievable requirements to be removed
    through endorsement .
*   There are no Exclusion Clauses which excludes the risk(s) required to be covered as mandated
    under Para 9.3.2 (unless deviation has been accorded as prescribed under Annexure FM: 9.17)

heading: 9.3.4 Industry-Wise Risk Coverage
content:
Please refer to Annexure FM: 9.16 reflecting industry-wise risk coverage for hypothecated / leased /
pledged stocks, plant & machinery and buildings (residential, commercial, factory and warehouse).
Business Unit to provide comprehensive Takaful / Insurance covering ALL risks for customer not
part of industry reflected in this Annexure FM: unless specific waiver for a particular RISK is
OBTAINED.

EXCEPTIONS TO ANNEXURE FM: 9.16 IS APPENDED BELOW:

It is ESSENTIAL to seek coverage against Aircraft Damage in the event the assets under MBL's
charge are in close proximity to Air force Base / Airport / Flying Zone.

Risk coverage against Atmospheric Disturbance is ESSENTIAL wherever MBL's encumbered assets
are located in geographical areas where heavy rainfall is a norm / close proximity to coastal areas
(e.g. Hawks bay and Sea View, Karachi).

Risk Coverage against Impact Damage is ESSENTIAL in the event MBL's encumbered assets are in
close proximity to highways or fast moving heavy vehicle / automotive traffic

Risk Coverage against Earthquake Shock / Fire Damage is ESSENTIAL in the event MBL's
encumbered assets are in geographical areas with prior history of earthquakes / earthquake
declared zones.

RISK COVERAGE against Aircraft Damage, Atmospheric Disturbance, Earthquake Shock / Fire
Damage and Impact Damage is ESSENTIAL as mentioned above (any deviation to be accorded as
prescribed under Annexure FM: 9.17).

For finance size up to Rs 1 million in case of Small Enterprise only, it will be at the discretion of the
approving authority as per DOA to obtain Insurance Cover of hypothecated stock/ other securities,
keeping in view the creditworthiness of the borrower, his past experience and financial strength.

heading: 9.3.5 Salient Features
content:
Salient features of Takaful / Insurance Policy acceptable to MBL

*   Genuineness confirmation of Takaful/Insurance and PPR should be confirmed by CAD within
    one month of receipt of insurance policy/PPR from the Takaful/Insurance Company.
*   Submission of partial premium payment receipts to be acceptable in the event the premium
    amount matches with that reflected in the payment schedule provided by the respective
    insurance company. In the event PPR is subject to/ conditional upon realization of cheque CAD
    / Business Unit to seek confirmation from respective Takaful / Insurance Company on its
    REALIZATION (since Takaful / Insurance coverage becomes effective upon realization of
    cheque).
*   Deferred Payment Schedule (for acceptance please refer to Annexure FM: # 9.17).
*   Amount insured by Takaful / Insurance company / co-insurers is within the approved per risk
    limits circulated by FI's. (Any deviation to be waived through FI's).
*   Per Party limit of Insurance/Takaful Company and that of co-insurers to be within per risk
    limits approved by FI's before implementing limits.
*   In case of co-insurance/Takaful, share of each Insurance/Takaful company is authenticated by
    co-insurers.
*   No deductable Clause (any deviation to be accorded as prescribed in Annexure FM: # 9.17)
*   The share of each insurance company as part of a Takaful / Insurance policy must be mentioned
    and authenticated in case of Joint Policy and share of individual Takaful / Insurance Company
    not to exceed Per Risk Limit circulated by Financial Institutions Department.
*   In case of Ijarah Assets the cost of Insurance / Takaful coverage to be borne by MBL (Lessor) and
    the same recovered from Lessee (customer) through Ijarah rentals.
*   In addition to coverage of risks mentioned in Para 9.3.2 and 9.3.3 the financing approving
    authority may require additional risks to be covered on case-to-case basis depending upon the
    nature of business and risk profile of the customer.
*   FULL COVERGAE of BANKS INVENTORY under SPOT Murabaha, Tijarah. Istisna, DM &
    Ijarah etc. (any deviation to be accorded as prescribed under Annexure FM: # 9.17)
*   Business Unit to provide endorsement in the event of any Change in location of security from
    that reflecting in the Insurance/Takaful policy.
*   Open Pledge MUST be adequately covered through Takaful / Insurance policy and policy
    should clearly mention stocks/assets are stored in open and there should be no restrictive clause
    regarding such storage arrangement to avoid any dispute in the event of any claim
*   Business Unit must provide proper justifications/reasoning for any waiver in Takaful/Insurance
    Policy to respective approving authority.
*   CAD to maintain and update Proper log of amendments on record.
*   Coverage of stocks in process to be obtained, wherever applicable.
*   Coverage of stocks in transit to be obtained, wherever applicable.
*   In case of pari-passu status involving multiple financers, the policy must be assigned in favor of
    the financing banks. In case of any amendments, the same must be communicated/updated to
    the co-bankers.
*   In case of syndicate / sukuk financing where held security is insured in favor of lead bank /
    agent bank, without joint charge of other consortium banks, the certified true copy (CTC) of
    insurance/takaful policy must be obtained from lead arranger for assessment and record.
    Exception in such policies must be conferred with the lead arranger by business unit.
*   CAD to ensure ALL Excess Over Limits are allowed subject to confirmation that
    Insurance/Takaful coverage adequately covers assets securing the enhanced EOL amount for
    the extended time period.
*   Customer to get Takaful / Insurance coverage for all stocks/assets held so that in case of any
    mishap their loss may be minimized. Where customers do not get the remaining assets/stocks
    insured, an undertaking should be obtained from customers that Takaful claim received shall be
    first available towards adjustment of Bank's financing and balance if any shall be repaid / paid
    from their own sources (Subject to SCD concurrence in case of banks own assets)
*   As per existing standard clause in Takaful / Insurance policies covering Assets “If the Asset /
    property hereby covered shall at the breaking out of any fire be collectively of greater value than
    the sum covered thereon then the Participant shall be considered as bearing the Risk himself for
    the difference and shall bear a rate able proportion of the loss or damage accordingly. Every
    item, if more than one of the Policy shall be separately taken into consideration subject to this
    condition”.

    To further explain this clause we may assume Assets held by customer for Rs. 100 million while
    Takaful / Insurance shall be sought for Rs. 50 million to adequately secure Assets against
    financing facilities availed from MBL. In event of claim due to a destruction of Assets of Rs. 50
    million the insurer shall provide Claim to customer up to Rs. 25 million calculated on proportion
    of loss to insured amount

    In view of the above it is therefore mandatory for business units to ensure that Customer obtains
    Takaful / Insurance coverage for all Stocks/Assets held so that in case of any mishap claim is
    sufficient to cover MBL finance (any deviation to be accorded as only on exceptional basis as
    prescribed in Annexure FM: 9.17)
*   CAD to advise Business Units to write to the customer at least One (1) Month before the expiry
    of the Insurance/Takaful Policy requesting them to issue renewal instructions to the
    Insurance/Takaful company under copy to the Bank.
*   Takaful / Insurance policies to be renewed prior to expiry date
*   A reminder letter must be sent to the customer by the business unit on the advice from CAD at
    least 15 days before the expiry date of Insurance/Takaful policy.
*   Business unit to ensure outstanding exposure is covered under Takaful/Insurance policy (where
    applicable) in case of expired limits and where client is not ready to pay the Takaful / Insurance
    charges, approval for payment of premium to be also obtained from the DCEO / CEO through
    RAMD or Business Department (wherever the account is parked).
*   CAD/business unit/RAMD to ensure Takaful / Insurance coverage is in place on non-
    performing assets including which have been referred to legal counsel for recovery suit filed by
    Bank. CAD / Business Unit to seek advice of legal counsel contesting the case on Bank's behalf
    to seek court's permission to debit cost of this coverage to outstanding balances because the
    matter is subjudice or alternatively approval to pay premium from expense account to be
    obtained from DCEO / CEO through RAMD Department.

heading: 9.3.6 Fixed Assets
content:
Takaful / Insurance cover for building (including fixtures & fittings) to be for amount equivalent to
market value appraised by MBL approved valuator above plinth level. Value of land shall be
excluded to calculate the amount of Takaful / Insurance required.

heading: 9.3.7 Fire Coverage
content:
It is one of the Main Insurance Policy document. Fire Policy provides Takaful /Insurance coverage
to the Property / Assets insured if destroyed or damaged by Fire and / or Lightening.

In case of property the Takaful / Insurance Company may pay at market value at the time of
destruction / damage or at its option reinstate / replace such property or any part thereof.

It is necessary to obtain a Fire policy as all other risks under FIRE COVERAGE are covered by
extensions to this main policy and as such its terms & conditions apply to extensions as well, unless
varied other-wise.

Loss caused by Spontaneous combustion is not covered by Fire Policy unless an extension to this
effect is sought so it is prudent to obtain a Fire Policy with extension to cover loss caused by
Spontaneous Fire (i.e. against Cotton, gasoline etc.)

heading: 9.3.8 RSD Coverage
content:
Riot and Strike Endorsement is an extension of Fire Policy and provides risk coverage due to
damage or loss caused by following acts:

a) Strike or Lock-out
b) Action of any lawful constituted authority in suppressing or attempting to suppress any such
    disturbance or in minimizing the consequences of any such disturbance or in preventing or
    attempting to prevent any such act or in minimizing the consequences of any such act
c) The willful act of any striker or locked-out worker done in furtherance of a strike or in resistance
    to a lock-out

Loss to property caused by an employee in collusion with external assistance (i.e. outside customer's
premises) shall be covered by a separate terrorism policy.

RSD coverage is particularly required in the below-mentioned instances:

*   Stocks /Assets stored in Factory Premises
*   Disturbed areas / Shopping centers or during periods of political unrest
*   All other situations, where chances of loss due to such peril is significant

RSD endorsement DOES NOT provide coverage against loss caused by War, Mutiny, Hostilities,
Civil Commotion and Terrorism.

heading: 9.3.9 Malicious Damage
content:
Malicious damage shall mean all physical loss or damage resulting from a malicious act caused by
anyone whether or not the aforesaid act is committed during a disturbance of public peace, and shall
include loss caused by sabotage and terrorism meaning an act, including the use of force or violence,
of any person or group(s) of persons, whether acting alone or on behalf of or in connection with any
organization(s), committed for political, religious or ideological purposes including the intention to
influence any government and/or to put the public in fear for such purposes.

Malicious damage endorsement is an extension of RSD and extends coverage for loss or damage to
property directly caused by the malicious act of any person not due to War / Invasion / Civil
commotion / Terrorism etc.

Malicious Damage is particularly required in the following instances:

a) Flammable items or liquid cargo stored in drums / less durable tanks or where security system
    is inadequate.
b) Finance extended to traders / shopkeepers
c) Mortgaged property
d) Areas where feudal / competitive rivalry is significant

heading: 9.3.10 Aircraft Damage Endorsement
content:
This endorsement includes coverage due to loss or damage to property insured (by fire or
otherwise) directly caused by Aircraft and other aerial devices and / or articles dropped there from.
This coverage to remain in force provided the Main Fire Policy is valid and loss deemed to be by
fire.

This endorsement is particularly required for coverage of the following:

a) Location of Mortgaged Property / Stocks pledged or hypothecated is near to an Airport (civil or
    military) or if in the direction of flying course
b) Damage / Loss due to vibration of Aircraft's low flight over the premises

This endorsement DOES NOT provide coverage against any loss or damage caused by any Aircraft
to which permission to land has been extended by the Insured / loss exceeding insured amount.

heading: 9.3.12 Impact Damage endorsement
content:
This endorsement provides coverage against loss or damage to Building & / or its contents, gate,
boundary wall due to impact by any road vehicle not belonging to or under the control of the
insured.
It should be noted that any damage or loss caused to property by impact of road vehicle, belonging
to or under the control of the insured, is not covered under this extension.

heading: 9.3.13 Atmospheric Disturbance Endorsement
content:
This endorsement provides coverage against damage or loss from Heavy Rain, Snow, Hail, Wind,
Hurricane, Cyclone, Tornado, Flood and Typhoon.

This clause DOES NOT provide coverage against loss or damage due to

*   Normal rain or flood on account of normal water course or leakage from pipe / tap etc.
*   Goods in open and / or in open sided sheds / building and Underground tanks in the open
    containing solvents, fuel, oils, chemicals or any other liquid.

Therefore, it is imperative that movable and immovable assets are safe from normal rain.

heading: 9.3.14 Standard Explosion endorsement
content:
Standard Explosion Endorsement provides coverage for loss or damage to property by fire caused y explosion, occasioned by or through or in consequence, directly, of acts of terrorism (use of
violence for political ends and includes any use of violence for the purpose of putting the public or
any section of the public in fear.) committed by a person or persons acting on behalf of or in
connection with any organization

This policy should be used where probability of explosion is significant or in those industries where
obtaining of coverage for such peril is customary.

Please note that loss of or damage to boilers, economizers, or other vessels, machinery or apparatus
in which pressure is used or their contents resulting from their explosion is not covered. More
relevant to storage of flammable liquid or liquids stored in premises.

heading: 9.3.15 Earthquake Shock Endorsement
content:
Business Units are advised to ensure coverage particularly against this risk for areas falling in
earthquake zones or scientific reports reflecting possibility of earthquake.

heading: 9.3.16 Earthquake Fire Endorsement
content:
This Endorsement covers loss or damage by fire to any of the property insured by this policy
occasioned by or through or in consequence of earthquake.

heading: 9.3.17 Burglary
content:
Endorsement against burglary covers loss or damage by following acts:

*   Theft / Burglary or Housebreaking accompanied by actual forcible and violent breaking into or
    out of the premises provided the premises are guarded by armed guards.

Coverage against burglary is Only against those thefts which are followed by / consequent to
burglary. The deployment of round the clock Chowkidar / Guard with the standard condition that
Armed Chowkidar / Guard be posted by insured goods every night from 9.00 p.m. to 6.00 am may
be mandatory by the insurer.

Burglary endorsement is particularly required for coverage of the following:

a) Hypothecated / Pledge of stocks (including but not limited to stocks of sugar, cotton & other
    bulky items).
b) All Moveable goods or Unmovable / Assets which may be easily removed.

Burglary endorsement DOES NOT provide coverage against loss caused by Theft or any attempt by
any member of the insured's family, business staff, domestic servants, or any persons enters
lawfully on the premises whether such person or persons are concerned as principals or accessories.

heading: 9.3.18 Terrorism Coverage
content:
Terrorism is an extension of RSD and Takaful / Insurance companies are now providing two
separate policies for Terrorism coverage (details of Policy T3 and LPO 437) as mentioned below:

**9.3.18.1 Terrorism Policy LPO 437**

Terrorism Policy LPO 437 provides coverage in the event of Physical loss or damage arising from
riots and/or strikes and/or civil commotions including fire damage and loss by looting following
riots and/or strikes and/or civil commotion and/or malicious damage (e.g. riot & strikes that
commenced on Dec 27, 2007).

**9.3.18.2 Terrorism Policy Т3**

Terrorism Policy T3 provides coverage in the event of Physical loss or damage by use of force or
violence whether acting alone or on behalf or in conjunction with any organization, committed for
political, religious or ideological purposes including the intention to influence any government
and/or or to put the public in fear for such purposes (e.g. Marriot hotel explosion in Islamabad).

heading: 9.3.19 Approved Panel of Takaful/ Insurance Companies
content:
Takaful / insurance companies on MBL's panel to be reviewed on an annual basis by Financial
Institutions department as per the “F.I. Criteria for Limit Allocation of Insurance Companies”. Any
enlistment / delisting of a Takaful / Insurance company shall be duly approved through Financial
Institutions Dept. and updated list of Takaful / Insurance companies to be maintained with CAD
and Business Units.

Compliance with “Per Party Per Risk Limit” assigned to each Insurance company to be ensured by
CAD. The Per Party Per Risk limit is specific for General and Marine Coverage separately against a
Single Insurance Company.

The two Takaful /Insurance categories are mentioned below:

1) General Takaful / Insurance is any insurance other than Marine Insurance.
2) Marine Takaful / Insurance covers the loss or damage of ships, cargo, terminals, and any
   transport or cargo by which goods /assets is transferred, acquired, or held between the
   points of origin and final destination.

Please note that Limit Allocation to each Takaful / Insurance Company is mainly based on Credit
Rating, Financial Analysis, and Reinsurance Treaties as per approved policy followed by FI's.

heading: 9.3.20 Approval of Deductible Clause
content:
In case of Corporate Customers, Approval to accept the policies with Deductible Clause shall be
considered on a case to case basis for decision. The discretionary powers against Deductible clause/
per corporate client are as under:

1. Group Head Corporate Banking : Up-to PKR 0.100 Million
2. Deputy Chief Executive Officer : Above PKR 0.100 Million and up-to PKR 5.0 Million
3. President & Chief Executive Officer : Above PKR 5.0 Million

heading: 9.4.1 Deferral Policy
content:
It is the bank's policy to obtain complete, legally executed security documentation from obligors
prior to disbursement of facilities. All finances will be disbursed after completion of the required
security/ support documents. Therefore, deferral of finance documents will generally be
discouraged. There may however be genuine situations where deferral of financing documents may
be considered for disbursal of approved finance facilities for specific situation. The documentation
requirements have been classified in following three categories:

1. Documents providing evidence to legal claim
2. Documents required by the regulatory body; and
3. Support documents.

The first two categories represent "essential" documents and their deferral will not be allowed. A
brief list of such documents is mentioned in Annexure FM: 9.15.1. Support documents deferral may
be approved as mentioned in the preceding paragraphs.

heading: 9.4.2 Documentation Categories
content:
**1. Documents providing evidence to legal claim**

All documents that establish the Bank's rights and/or claims, evidence of disbursement of facilities
and creation of relevant securities are essential.

As a policy, all such documents that provide evidence to legal claim are not deferrable.

**2. Documents required by regulatory bodies**

All documents that are required to be obtained as per instructions issued by SBP/ any other
regulatory body are not deferrable.

**3. Support documents**

Documents that do not provide evidence to legal claim and are obtained to further strengthen
security interest or to monitor performance of the borrower are deferrable. A list of deferrable
documents is available at Annexure FM: 9.15.2.

heading: 9.4.3 Guidelines for Deferral Approving Authority other than CC
content:
While granting approval, it will be ensured that:

*   Deferral document do not fall under document category 1 & 2
*   Deferrals will not expose the Bank to any pecuniary risk and Bank's security position is not
    weakened. The deferral does not jeopardize the rights and remedies available to the Bank.
    While allowing deferrals, the approving authorities may obtain the advice of In-house Legal
    Department on need basis so as to ensure that deferrals do not result in compromising the
    Bank's interest.
*   Deferral does not violate Shar'iah guidelines issued by SCD from time to time. In case of any
    doubt/confusion in Shar'iah compliance issue, guidelines/approval to be obtained from
    SCD.
*   The deferral does not violate any of the regulatory requirements.
*   The customer has proven positive track record.
*   The customer has undertaken in writing to regularize the deferred documents within the
    stipulated time.
*   Completion of deferred documentation is certain/ most probable.
*   Deviation from SBP prudential regulations / any other regulations will require waiver from
    SBP. Such waiver request to be signed off by respective Business/Group Head & will be
    forwarded through Compliance Group for onward submission to SBP.
*   For deviation from SBP PRs / any other regulations, where bank at its own discretion can
    allow relaxation, approval/ review from President & CEO/ Credit Committee will be
    obtained.

heading: 9.4.4 Deferral Approval Authority
content:
Deferral Approval authorities are mentioned in the Annexure 9.15.2.

1st Deferrals will be allowed by relevant approving authority as per delegation matrix mentioned in
the annexure. If documentation is not perfected within the time frame conveyed for 1st deferral,
Business unit may elevate request for 2nd and/or 3rd deferral providing adequate justification in this
regard. Maximum time for 2nd & 3rd deferral would be same as specified in Annexure 9.15.2. No
deferral will be allowed by the higher level approving authority for the maximum number of days
within his authority without expiry of previous deferral e.g., no deferral may be allowed for
maximum 90 days in one go by the relevant approving authority without expiry of 1st and 2nd
deferrals of 30 days each.

Upon expiry of deferral, any deficiency in deferred documents will result in automatic limit
freezing.

Deferral for classified finances will be approved by CEO & DCEO on recommendation of RAMD/
Business Groups.

heading: 9.4.5 Deferral Requests
content:
Relationship Managers/ branches may use the attached format (Annexure FM: 9.15.3) for obtaining
deferral of any document. Proper reasons for deferral requirement should be provided with the
request. In case request is forwarded electronically, they should incorporate all relevant information.

heading: 9.4.6 Procedural Requirements
content:
The responsibility for obtaining complete documents from an obligor/ group lie with the respective
Relationship manager/ Branch Manager, whereas CAD is responsible for lodgment and control of
security documents. When accepting security documentation from an obligor, the CAD must ensure
that documents are executed on the Bank's standard approved forms, and checks the same for
completeness and enforceability. Where security documentation is incomplete, or any discrepancies,
and only as exception, a deferral/ waiver may be requested from the appropriate authority by
Business Unit.

While initiating a deferral, the RM will prepare a Deferral Request Form (DRF) as per attached
format wherein reasons / justifications for the proposed deferral should be clearly identified. The
deferral should be routed to the approval authority supported by CAD intimation for the requested
deferral. After approval, the DRF will be forwarded to the CAD.

heading: 9.4.7 Monitoring & Reporting
content:
The deferral approval will be forwarded to CAD who would allow disbursement after
    confirming that all documentation including any required deferrals is in place.
*   The CAD will maintain a record of deferrals and intimate concerned RM/ Business unit of
    outstanding deferral through the monthly documentation deferred status report.
*   All deferrals will be reported in the monthly Documentation Deferral Reports generated by
    CAD.
*   CAD will submit a consolidated documentation deferral status report on a monthly basis for
    review by CC.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.1 Eligible Collateral acceptable by Bank for financing (part 1)
content:
Annexure FM: 9.1 Eligible Collateral acceptable by Bank for financing:
[TABLE START]
Sr. # | Type | Examples | Type of Charge
A | Immovable Properties | Fixed Assets Land, Building, Machinery (immovable) | Mortgage/ Fixed/ Floating Charge
B | Movable Properties
  | i) Tangibles | Stocks/ Raw Material/ Finished Good/Plant & Machinery/ Commodities | Hypothecation/ Pledge/Floating Charge
  | ii) Intangibles | Receivables, book debts | Hypothecation/ Assignment

  | | Other Banks Deposits, Deposit Receipts, COI etc. (Pak Rs.) | Lien & pledge of acceptable deposits/certificates duly discharged
  | | Other Islamic Bank Deposit (FCY) |
  | | SBLC's or guarantees of Banks for which FID line allocation is obtained | Guarantees having transferable/ endorsable clause, & genuineness checked
  | | MBL Assets Management Funds | Lien & in case of receipt pledge duly discharged & signature verified
C | Other Forms of Collateral | Personal Guarantees, Financial/ Corporate Guarantees |
  | | Any other collateral that do not fall under any category |
[TABLE END]
**Collateral not acceptable as security**
- Items specifically banned by SBP.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.1 Eligible Collateral acceptable by Bank for financing (part 2)
content:
- Items whose trade declared illegal by Government.
- Properties/ Securities in the name of Minor or trusts (except permissible to offer collateral in trust deed) and acceptable to legal department/insane person.
- Precious stones, gems, antique etc. (Those with highly fluctuating value) Gold, Jewelry, ornaments (including artificial/ imitated jewelry etc.
**Eligible Collateral under Basel II**
Bank is following standardized approach (Simple Approach) for calculation of capital charge under Basel II. Please refer to Annexure FM: 5.1.9 for details regarding eligible collateral under Basel II.
Under simple approach, where a transaction is secured by eligible collateral and meets the eligibility criteria and minimum requirements, banks are allowed to reduce their exposure under that particular transaction by taking into account the risk mitigating effect of the collateral for the calculation of capital requirement
The operational and legal requirements have been built in this chapter regarding eligible collateral under simple approach

heading: Annexure FM: 9.4 Calculation of Margin (part 1)
content:
Annexure FM: 9.4 Calculation of Margin
This Appendix provides methods of calculating margin requirements for:
Prime Collateral (Hypothecation/ Pledge of stocks/ Receivable) and Cash/ Near Cash Collateral
Secondary Collateral (Fixed Assets/ Property)
Non-Fund Based financing
Margin requirement in case of Prime Collateral
Prime Collateral refers to Hypothecation/ Pledge of stocks/ Receivable/shares and Cash/ Near Cash Collateral.
Example:
If finance of Rs.100M is required to be disbursed at 25% Margin, the value of required Prime Collateral shall be calculated using the following formula:
Prime Collateral required (Value) = Finance Amount × 100 ÷ (100 - Margin)
Calculation:
Prime Collateral required Value = 100 × 100 ÷ (100 - 25)
Prime Collateral required Value = PKR 133.333 Million
Margin / Coverage Requirement in case of Secondary Collateral
Secondary Collateral refers to Fixed Assets / Property.
Situation 1:
Where Prime Collateral is hypothecation of Stocks/ Receivables and type of financing falls under mortgage-based financing category.
Example:
Limit / Finance Amount: PKR 200 M
Margin + 30%
Calculation of Requirement of Secondary Collateral in shape of Property / Fixed Assets:
Secondary Collateral required (Value) = Finance Amount × 100 ÷ (100 - Margin)
Result:
Secondary Collateral required Value = 200 × 100 ÷ (100 - 30)
Secondary Collateral required Value = PKR 285.714 Million
Situation 2:
Where Prime Collateral offered is Pledge of stocks.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.4 Calculation of Margin (part 2)
content:
Example:
Pledge Based Limit / Finance Amount = PKR 150 M
Collateral Coverage Required = 25%
Calculation of Requirement of Secondary Collateral in shape of Property / Fixed Assets:
Secondary Collateral required (Value) = Finance × Collateral Coverage ÷ 100
Result:
Secondary Collateral required Value = 150 × 25 ÷ 100
Secondary Collateral required Value = PKR 37.5 Million
Margin Requirement in case of Non-Fund Based Financing
In case of non-fund financing, the margin amount is calculated using the following formula:
Margin Amount in case of Non-Fund Exposure = Non-Fund Exposure × Margin (As per Approval) ÷ 100

content:
Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables
MEEZAN BANK LIMITED
In consideration of MEEZAN BANK LTD an Islamic banking company incorporated under the laws of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and having its registered office at at Meezan House C-25, Estate Avenue, sale proceeds thereof (hereinafter referred to as "stocks") and all its present and future book debts, outstandings, monies, receivables, claims, bills, contracts, engagements, securities and rights (all of which are hereinafter referred to as the receivables) by way of continuing security for securing the discharge to you of all monies and liabilities now or hereafter due or owing from or incurred by us upon any account or any manner whatsoever and arising under or pursuant to the relevant financing agreement(s) executed and/or to be executed from time to time between ourselves and the Bank (hereinafter referred to as "the Financing Agreement(s)") and whether accrued, accruing, or contingent including financial loss (if any, excluding opportunity cost of fund) and all costs, charges, and expenses incurred in protecting, obtaining and maintaining possession of the stocks and receivables comprised in the security or in protecting, enforcing or releasing this security or for any advice as to the Banks legal position in connection with the security hereby created and we agree and undertake as follows:
1.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables (part 2)
content:
We shall hold as trustee and in trust for you the stocks comprised in this security as your exclusive property and we hereby undertake forthwith to bring to and keep the said stocks at Company's godowns situated at Company premises and/or in transit and/or stored elsewhere in Pakistan and we shall not (except as hereinafter stated) at any time so long as there shall be any balance due or owing by us or any of them on any account remove or cause or permit to be removed from the said premises or godowns or divert or deal with to the detriment of the Bank or hypothecate or otherwise charge or encumber any of the stocks or do or permit any act whereby the security herein expressed to be given shall be in any manner impaired or the interest of the Bank therein shall be adversely or prejudicially affected in any manner.
2. Until you shall otherwise by writing direct or demand payment of any sums hereby secured we are to be at liberty from time to time in the ordinary course of business to sell or ship any of the said stocks provided that the proceeds of all stocks sold shall be paid to the Bank in reduction of our indebtedness to you.
3. All bills of exchange drawn by us in respect of the proceeds of sale of any stocks comprised in this security and accompanying documents of title (if any) shall be placed in your possession for realization.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables (part 3)
content:
4. As and when any stocks comprised in this security shall be sold or shipped we will substitute the same or add further goods and all documents of title thereto and the stocks and documents as aforesaid so substituted and the sale proceeds thereof with the stocks comprised in this security not sold or shipped and documents as aforesaid shall be hypothecated and charged to you hereunder and be comprised in this security and in cases where railway receipts, delivery orders or other documents of title to stocks are deposited with you the relative stocks referred to therein shall be hypothecated and charged to the Bank and form part of this security.
5. We undertake always to keep hypothecated and charged to you hereunder stocks and/or relative documents so as to maintain always, either by payment in reduction of the liability secured hereunder or by additions thereto stocks of adequate value so that the total amount of the liability secured hereunder from time to time however arising shall never exceed 75% of value of such stocks. The value aforesaid shall be the current market value of which you will be the sole judge or landed cost whichever is less.
6. The stocks shall be insured and kept insured by us against loss or damage by fire, explosion, lightning, theft, insurrection, riot and civil commotion and against such other risks as you may from time to time require and such takaful shall be effected with a takaful company approved by you to the extent of the full market value of the stocks and the policies for such takaful shall be taken in your name and delivered forthwith to you, and we undertake punctually to pay the premium due for such takaful(s) and to deliver the premium receipts to you and should we fail so to insure or keep insured the stocks and/or to deliver such policies and receipts, you shall be at liberty but not bound to effect any such takaful(s) at our expense.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables (part 4)
content:
7. If we shall receive any sums under any takaful relating to the stocks we shall pay the said sums to you immediately on receiving the same and in the meantime we shall hold the said sums as trustee and in trust for you.
8.
9. If the stocks are stored in a godown owned or occupied by us, we expressly undertake that such godown shall not contain any goods belonging to or charged to or forming the security of any other bank or third party.
10. We will render to you statements giving descriptions and quantities at the end of each month/quarter with particulars of takaful thereon of all stocks sold or shipped during such month/quarter and of all stocks substituted or added during such month/quarter. Such statement shall be in such form and give such particulars as you may reasonably require. We also authorize you and your representatives to inspect and take particulars at any time or times of the stocks or any of them and if you think fit to have all or any of them valued at our expense by a valuer appointed by you. We also hereby undertake to furnish and verify all statements, reports, accounts, documents and information, to execute all documents and to do all things which you may require in relation to the stocks and/or the receivables to give effect to the security created hereunder.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables (part 5)
content:
11. In the event of our being in default in any of our obligations hereunder or in the event of our failing or neglecting to pay on demand all sums due or owing from us whether on account of purchase price, cost, principal or profit or other return or financial loss (except opportunity cost of fund), or compensation or charges, outlays or other expenditure, or any part thereof, or on the occurrence of any circumstances in your opinion endangering this security, and so often as such event or occurrence shall happen and so long as any such default, neglect or circumstances shall continue, you shall have the full, free and unfettered right at our risk and expenses as to the whole or any part of the stocks and so that the exercise of one power shall not prevent the exercise of any other powers hereby or in law conferred upon you:
a) to appoint by writing signed by any manager, assistant manager, acting manager or acting assistant manager of your bank one or more receivers (with power to you to remove or substitute them or any of them) as our agents to demand, collect or recover the stocks or their value and the income and sale proceeds thereof by suit or otherwise and to exercise such of the powers vested in you in relation to the stocks as you may from time to time direct, for such remuneration (not exceeding 10 (ten) percent of the gross collection) as you may think reasonable and the receivers shall apply all moneys received by them, firstly in discharge of all costs, charges and expenses incurred by them as receivers, secondly in payment of their remuneration, thirdly in or towards payment of all moneys owing to you from us however arising and whether due or not, and fourthly, if thereafter there remains any surplus it shall be paid to us, and/or
b) to seize, take possession of and to sell or otherwise dispose of the stocks or any part thereof at such time or times with or without reserve in whole or in lots (and without regard to the amount actually due to you) and in such fashion whether by public auction or private bargain and at such price or prices as you may in your absolute discretion consider expedient, without being bound to exercise any of these powers or being liable for any loss in the exercise thereof and without prejudice to the Bank's rights and remedies of suit or otherwise and not withstanding there may be pending any suit or other proceedings and we undertake to give you any receivers whom you may appoint all facilities necessary or in your opinion expedient for enforcing this security including such possession or information as you may require for that purpose.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables (part 6)
content:
12. In the event of the sale or other disposition by you of the whole or any part of the stocks or the receipt by you of the whole or any part of the money due under all or any of the said takafuls the proceeds thereof shall be applied firstly, in payment of the expenses of and incidental to the realization and recovery of the proceeds of sale or disposal or takaful, secondly, in payment of all disbursements made by you in relation to the stocks and/or receivables, thirdly in or towards payment in accordance with the Financing Agreement(s) of all monies owing to you from us however arising and whether due or not, and fourthly, if thereafter there remains any surplus it shall be paid to us and if there be a shortfall we undertake to pay it to you in cash on demand.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.1 Letter of Hypothecation of Stocks & Receivables (part 7)
content:
14. You shall be entitled at our risk and expenses to take possession and/or appoint receivers of any of the receivables under this security, to give notices to make demand on debtors and third parties liable therefore to sue for, recover/receive and give receipts for the same, and to otherwise dispose of all or any part of the receivables and to enforce, settle, compromise, submit to arbitration or deal in any manner with any of such receivables under this security, and to complete any engagements, under this security, without being bound to exercise any of these powers or liable for any loss in the exercise thereof, and without prejudice to your rights and remedies of suit against us and/or our guarantors.

Subject to your powers and our obligations herein contained and until you shall otherwise by writing direct or demand payment of any sums hereby secured we shall be at liberty to deal with the receivables in the ordinary course of business provided that all monies received by us in respect thereof shall be paid to you in reduction of our indebtedness to you.

content:

**Letter of Hypothecation of Movables & Receivables**
MEEZAN BANK LIMITED
DHA Phase II (Extension) Branch,
Karachi
In consideration of MEEZAN BANK LTD a banking company incorporated under the laws of the Islamic Republic of
Pakistan and having its registered office at Meezan House C-25, Estate Avenue, SITE, Karachi having provided or
agreed to provide from time to time in its absolute discretion finances, investments, financial accommodation and

hereby hypothecate

to you all our movable assets of whatsoever nature now or hereafter belonging to us and without limiting the
generality of the foregoing the movable assets specified in the Schedule hereunder wherever they may be (including

or incurred by us upon any account or any manner whatsoever and arising under or pursuant to the relevant
financing agreement(s) executed and/or to be executed from time to time between ourselves and the Bank (hereinafter

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.3 Letter of Hypothecation of Movables & Receivables (part 2)

content:

heading: Annexure FM: 9.5.3 Letter of Hypothecation of Movables & Receivables (part 5)
content:

time or times with or without reserve in whole or in lots (and without regard to the amount actually due to
you) and in such fashion whether by public auction or private bargain and at such price or prices as you may
in your absolute discretion consider expedient, without being bound to exercise any of these powers or being
liable for any loss in the exercise thereof and without prejudice to the Bank's rights and remedies of suit or

content:
Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement
THIS AGREEMENT is made and entered into this _______________________________________________ banking company incorporated under the laws of Pakistan and having its registered office at Plot # C-25, Meezan
House, Estate Avenue, Site, Karachi, (hereinafter referred to as "MBL") of the ONE PART,
AND
M/s Muccadamage firm., a company having its principal place of business at Address of
Muccadamage firm. (hereinafter referred to as 'Mucaddam-Agent') of the OTHER PART.
WHEREAS MBL has, inter-alia, at the request of the Muccadam-Agent agreed to entrust to the Muccadam-Agent
stocks of finished goods (hereinafter referred to as "pledged goods") for the purpose of holding the same in trust on
behalf of MBL as its Agent, and for the benefit of and at the disposal of MBL;
AND WHEREAS MBL has informed the Muccadam-Agent that the pledged goods that may be handed over to the
Muccadam-Agent for storage shall be stocks of Description of Goods, pledged to MBL by M/S. ABC COMPANY
(the "customer") as security for repayment of the banking facilities extended by MBL to the customer;
AND WHEREAS the Muccadam-Agent has agreed to act as an agent and muccadam of MBL and to hold the
pledged goods in trust for the benefit of MBL as its agent and to act in relation thereto strictly under and in terms
of written instructions of MBL and as per the terms of this Agreement;
AND WHEREAS the parties are desirous of recording the terms and conditions of this Agreement in writing.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement (part 2)
content:
BETWEEN Meezan Bank Limited, a
NOW, THEREFORE THIS AGREEMENT WITNESSETH AS UNDER:
1. That with effect from ____________________the Muccadam-Agent shall act as the agent and muccadam of MBL
for the purpose of storage and handling of pledged goods as and when the same are pledged to MBL by the
customer to secure payment of financial facilities extended by MBL to the customer. In this regard the
Muccadam-Agent shall act as agent of MBL and hold the pledged goods and any documents of title thereto in
trust for the benefit of and at the disposal of MBL.
2. The Muccadam-Agent shall take utmost care of the pledged goods as is required under the law of bailee and
shall ensure that the pledged goods are not exposed to any danger of destruction, damage, deterioration or loss
on any account whatsoever.
3. The Muccadam-Agent shall employ sufficient number of staff, including armed guards on a revolving basis so
that the pledged goods are kept under surveillance at all times and protected against robbery, theft and
pilferage.
4. The Muccadam-Agent shall ensure that all the pledged goods, as are brought into the warehouse/godown are
inspected, counted and inventory thereof is prepared and furnished to MBL within 24 hours of the arrival and
storage thereof.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement (part 3)
content:
Similarly when any of the pledged goods are removed from the warehouse/godown against
cash payment pursuant to written delivery orders of MBL, the quantity sought to be removed shall be
inspected and counted and an inventory taken in respect thereof which shall be furnished to MBL within 24
hours of such removal.
5. The Muccadam-Agent shall not permit the removal of any of the pledged goods from the warehouse/godown
by any person(s) and no delivery shall be given of any quantity or otherwise to any person(s) without a written
delivery order issued by MBL duly signed by two authorized officers whose specimen signatures shall be
provided to the Muccadam-Agent and further provided that the delivery order is accompanied by an official
letter of MBL requesting the release and delivery of the specified quantity of pledged goods all of which should
bear the official seal/stamp of MBL and the Muccadam-Agent shall ensure that all deliveries are made against
cash payments unless otherwise instructed by MBL.
6. In addition to the inspection, inventory and reporting of incoming and outgoing pledged goods referred to
hereinabove, the Muccadam-Agent shall furnish to MBL a monthly stock report of the pledged goods stored in
the godown/warehouse.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement (part 4)
content:
7. The Muccadam-Agent shall indemnify and hold MBL indemnified against all claims, liabilities, losses and
damages that may arise or be sustained on any account whatsoever as a result of any loss or damage and/or
destruction of the pledged goods on any account whatsoever including loss on account of robbery, theft,
pilferage howsoever caused by any person(s) including the employees/guards/agents of the Muccadam-Agent
and/or on account of any lapse, negligence or other failing or lack of due care and control on the part of the
Muccadam-Agent or any other reason whatsoever.
8. The Muccadam-Agent shall not permit the customer/owners and/or any other person(s) except its own
employees, staff, guards and agents to enter the godown/warehouse where the pledged goods are stored
except with the prior written permission of MBL.
9. The Muccadam-Agent shall not enter into any contract or any business relationship or other dealings with the
customer of MBL whose goods are pledged to MBL.
10. The Muccadam-Agent does hereby confirm agree and declare that it recognizes the undisputed right of MBL to
the pledged goods stored in the godown/warehouse under and in terms of this Agreement and that MBL shall
have complete and unrestricted control of the pledged goods stored in the godown/warehouse with complete
right of disposition, removal and sale thereof and that the Muccadam-Agent shall at all times comply with and
carry out all orders and directives of MBL in relation to the pledged goods without any reference to the
customer/owners of the pledged goods and that the Muccadam-Agent shall assist MBL in exercising its rights
as pledgee of the pledged goods, as are available under the law and in terms of this Agreement.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement (part 5)
content:
11. The Muccadam-Agent confirms and declares that it shall employ for the purpose of storage and performance
of all obligations hereunder, all such staff, employees, guards who have adequate experience and expertise in
the nature of work and services to be rendered so that the management - care - custody and control of the
pledged goods is entrusted to qualified and experienced staff and employees including guards.
12. For all practical and legal purposes the Muccadam-Agent shall be responsible and answerable to MBL in
respect of the pledged goods and all other goods, stocks, commodities and articles brought and stored in the
warehouse/godown under and in terms of this Agreement all of which the Muccadam-Agent shall hold in
trust for the benefit of MBL and deal with or dispose off the same strictly in accordance with the written
instructions of MBL.
13. MBL shall pay to the Muccadam-Agent the charges to be mutually agreed upon between the parties in respect
of service provided by the Muccadam-Agent hereunder.
14. Insurance in respect of the pledged goods, shall be obtained by the customer/owners of the pledged goods in
their names but all such policies of insurance shall specify MBL as payee of the sum insured in the event of
loss or damage.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement (part 6)
content:
The Muccadam-Agent shall at all times hold in its record and furnish to MBL copies of such
policies of insurance and in the event of any policy not being obtained or being about to expire or lapse, shall
give immediate intimation thereof to MBL so as to enable them to obtain necessary insurance cover and if so
instructed by MBL the Muccadam-Agent shall take steps to obtain necessary insurance cover as aforesaid to
protect against any loss, damage or destruction of the pledged goods stored in the godown/warehouse.
15. MBL may in its absolute discretion terminate this agreement by giving 30 days notice to the Muccadam-
Agent. In the event of such termination by MBL the Muccadam-Agent will handover and deliver all the
pledged goods and/or other goods, stocks, commodities and articles as the case may be to MBL, its agents or
representatives on such day as may be intimated by MBL without any let or hindrance.
16. All the terms and condition of this Agreement shall be binding upon the customer who has agreed to be
bound by same.
17. The customer hereby undertakes to provide warehousing facilities/godowns or other premises for the
exclusive purpose of the storage of the pledged goods and the customer undertakes to ensure that the
warehouse/godown shall be completely under the custody and control of the Muccadam-Agent in all respects
and shall provide adequate locks on all means of access to the godown/warehouse to be kept under the
control of the Muccadam-Agent at all times.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.6.2 Mucaddamage Agreement (part 7)
content:
18. The customer shall further ensure that the Muccadam-Agent has unrestricted right of entry and exit to and
from the godown including the right to bring and/or revise all or any of the pledged goods therefrom and that
the warehouse/godown is protected and controlled by their authorized staff and employees.
19. THIS AGREEMENT relates to storage in the premises of the customer situated at godown/warehouse as may
be instructed by MBL.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF the parties have executed this Agreement of this day, month and year first above written.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge (part 1)
content:
Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge
To:
Meezan Bank Limited
Meezan House Plot No. C-25,
Estate Avenue SITE,
Karachi
Dear Sirs,
1. In consideration of your having at my/our request, granted/agreed to grant financial accommodation and
banking facilities to M/S. _____________________________, (hereinafter referred to as the 'Customer"), I/we do hereby
pledge, all such movables more particularly described in the schedule hereunder (hereinafter referred to as
2. "the pledged goods") as security for the payment/repayment of any and all sum(s), amount(s), dues owing to
you or which may at any time hereafter become due to you from me/us/Customer up to a maximum of
Rs. _________________ - (Rupees ___________________________ Only) plus service charges and all costs, charges and expenses
payable to and / or incurred by you.
3. You shall be at liberty to have the pledged goods valued by an appraiser to be appointed by you at any time
and from time to time and the fees and expenses of every such appraisement shall be debited to my/our
account, and shall be recoverable as provided in Para (1) above.
4. I/We shall keep or cause to be kept a register of the pledged goods for the time being and from time to time
pledged with you wherein I/we shall duly and punctually enter or cause to be entered particulars of all
pledged goods and of all goods and merchandise consumed there form and I/we shall, monthly or as often as
you may require, furnish to you a certified statement or copy of all entries which shall have been made in the
said register since the last statement or copy was furnished and shall, as often as may be required, produce
to you, your nominees or agents, the said register all accounts and other books, invoices, bills, vouchers,
instruments and paper in any way relating to the pledged good or any part thereof and shall permit you, your
nominees and agents to inspect and take copies of or extracts from the same and shall furnish to you, your
nominees and agents all such other particulars of or information concerning the pledged goods as you may
require.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge (part 2)
content:
5. I/We agree that you shall not be responsible/liable in respect of the pledged goods nor for counting,
measurement, quality, quantity etc. I/we shall hold you your nominees and agents harmless, free from any
liability/responsibility and fully indemnified against all losses, injury, damage or deterioration/depreciation
that may be caused to the pledged goods as a consequence or result, however remote, of any cause whatever,
including fire, storm, tempest, earthquake, rain, floods, riots, civil commotion, rebellion, insurrection and acts
of God or the enemies of the state, strikes, lockouts, political or labor disturbance, theft, misappropriation or
embezzlement or any other cause whatsoever notwithstanding the fact of your possession of the same or
otherwise and if the pledged goods shall at any time suffer any reduction/shortage or diminution in their
market value as a consequence or result of any such cause as aforesaid, or by virtue of shortage of goods
under pledge or if any shortage is found or alleged whether during your possession or upon re-delivery, you
shall not be liable or responsible for the same and I/we shall forthwith upon demand made by you deposit
with you further securities in the manner and to the extent of shortfall in the value of the same.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge (part 3)
content:
6. I/We shall at all times regularly and punctually pay all rents, rates, taxes and other impositions and outgoings
and shall duly discharge and comply with all orders and requirements of appropriate authorities that may
from time to time respectively become due and payable by me/us or be made upon me/us in respect of any
building or place wherein the pledged goods may be stored.
7. I/We shall at all times during the continuation of this pledge and so long as any money shall remain due and
owing to you insure and keep insured all the pledged goods to the full extent of their value against fire, theft
and all other risks, that you may require, with such insurance company as may be approved by you and in
your name and shall duly and punctually pay the premium payable in respect thereof at least one week before
the same shall become due or payable and shall hand over the policy or policies of insurance and receipts for
premium paid in respect thereof to you. I/We agree not to raise at any time any dispute as to the amount of
your insurable interest. If default be made in payment of such premium or in keeping the pledged goods so
insured, then and in such case it shall be lawful but not obligatory upon you to pay such premium and to
keep the same so insured and expenses incurred by you for the purpose shall be charged to and paid by
me/us, as if the same were part of the amount due to you.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge (part 4)
content:
8. I/We agree that in so far as I am / we are party/parties to this agreement by way of surety or guarantor, you
may enter into any contract with the principal debtor/Customer for the purpose of giving time for payment or
for any other purpose without prejudice to your rights against me/us as such surety(ies) or guarantor(s).
9. Should the total amount of all existing outstanding at any time exceed a sum in excess of _% of the value on
the aforesaid goods, bills of lading, warrants, delivery orders and documents of title and securities whatsoever
and the property which is the subject matter thereof valued at the current market prices or upon the contract
prices or any combination of the current market prices and the contract prices as you alone may determine,
that I/we undertake on receipt of a notice in writing to that effect from you to pay within twenty-four hours of
the date of such notice such sum as shall reduce the amount outstanding to a sum such as you may alone
direct and determine and if in default then I/we agree that your power of selling all or any of the pledged
goods of assigning, transferring or negotiating the said bills of lading warrants, delivery orders and documents
of title and securities whatsoever shall be immediately exercisable with or without notice to us and I/we
furthermore agree to repay immediately any liability still outstanding after such sale.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge (part 5)
content:
10. That if for any reason whatsoever it shall be necessary or you shall require that the said goods when pledged
and stored be removed to another godown or place then I/we will pay to you on demand the total cost of the
removal and re-storage thereof and until payment the said goods shall stand pledged as security thereof.
11. I/we undertake to sign execute and deliver any transfers, deeds or documents which you may require me/us
to sign execute and deliver for perfecting your title to the said securities or pledged goods or property and/or
for vesting the same in or delivering the same to any purchaser or purchasers from you.
12. You shall be entitled to adjust, settle, compromise or refer to arbitration any dispute between any insurance
company and the insured arising under or in connection with any such policy or policies as aforesaid and
such adjustment, settlement, compromise and any award made on such arbitration shall be valid and binding
on me/us and you shall be entitled to receive all moneys payable under any such policy or under any claim
made there under and to give a valid receipt therefore and the amount so received shall be credited towards
our outstandings and I/we shall not raise any objection whatsoever in this regard.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.7 Letter of Pledge (part 6)
content:
13. In default of payment/repayment of any moneys hereby secured or in the performance of any obligations
hereunder, you shall be entitled to sell the pledged goods or any part thereof either by public auction or
private treaty including the right to acquire the same yourself.
14. I/We confirm that the pledged goods are my/our absolute property and are at my/our sole disposal, free from
any prior charge/lien or encumbrance and that all future goods and merchandise to be pledged hereafter
shall be likewise my/our sole unencumbered, absolute and disposable property.
15. Any notice by way of request, demand or otherwise may be given to me/us by leaving the same at our
premises, sending the same by post to my/our registered office or principal place of business in Pakistan,
where applicable and any sent send by post shall be deemed to have been given at the time when it would be
delivered in due course of post and in proving such notice when given by post, it shall be sufficient to prove
that the envelope containing the notice was posted and a certificate signed by your officer that the envelope
was so posted, shall be conclusive.
16. This Letter of Pledge shall be governed by the prevailing laws of Pakistan.

ANNEXURE: CHAPTER 9
Documents providing evidence to legal claim:
The following documents categorized as "compulsory" must be obtained prior to disbursement and eannot be
deferred.
1. Facility Offer Letter for new financing relationships and enhancements in facilities to existing financing
relationships, duly accepted by the obligor¹.
2. Financing Agreements
3. Charge documentation such as Letter of Hypothecation over Current Assets, Agreement to execute
Mortgage Deed, Memorandum of Deposit of Title Deed.
4. Obligors' Board resolution cannot be deferred. However, a circular Board Resolution may be
considered acceptable for Disbursement Advice/Transaction Approval Sheet (TAS) issuance purposes,
provided the same is replaced by a proper resolution within 90 days of the issuance of the TAS.
5. Memorandum & Articles of Association (M&A). The M & A in case of a limited liability company must
carry a clause authorizing the company to borrow.
6. Documents evidencing filing of charges, such as Acknowledgement of Filing issued by SECP.
Documents required by the regulatory body
1. Borrowers Basic Fact Sheet & CIB Report
● BBFS on prescribed format to be obtained (If LAF already contains all the information as required in
BBFS, no separate BBFS is required in case of SE)
● eCIB Report
2.Personal Guarantees (Prudential Regulation SME R-3)
● All facilities except those secured against liquid assets, to be secured against Personal Guarantees of
Proprietors / Partners / Directors (other than nominee directors)
3. Proper Utilization of Loan (Prudential Regulation SME R-5)
● Declaration for proper utilization of finance to be obtained from the customer
4. Restriction on Facilities to Related Parties (Prudential Regulation SME R-6)
● An undertaking from the customer stating that there is no existence of any interest between the
customer and related parties (as mentioned in PR's) to be obtained
---
¹ Document will be considered as compulsory if disbursement is being carried out in enhanced facility. For example if there has
been enhancement in funded facilities, whereas customer wants to open an LC, then the Offer letter will not be considered as a
compulsory document. However if the customer has been offered enhancement in kibor financing and he wants to avails the
same, then the OL will be considered part of Compulsory documents.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.16 Pertinent Risk Guidelines (part 1)
content:
This document is Annexure FM: 9.16 Pertinent Risk Guidelines.
It serves as a comprehensive matrix to identify the minimum insurance or risk coverage required for different types of assets and industries against specific perils.
The chart is organized with Risk Types across the top and Asset Categories down the left side.
1. Risk Categories (Columns)
These are the specific hazards the guidelines cover.
They include:
Physical Perils: Fire, Burglary, Earthquake Fire Risk, and Earthquake Shock.
Human-Induced Risks: Riots & Strikes, Malicious Damage, and Terrorism.
Environmental & External Risks: Atmospheric Disturbances, Aircraft Damage, Impact Damage, and Electrical issues.
2. Asset & Industry Categories (Rows)
The table breaks down requirements into three main groups:
Commodities
Pledge/Hypothecation: Covers basic perils like Fire and Burglary, but notes that further coverage depends on location and storage conditions.
Plant & Machinery
This is the most detailed section, listing specific industrial sectors:
Textile related: Ginning, Spinning/Weaving/Knitting, and Garments.
Food & Agriculture: Flour Mills, Sugar/Rice Mills, Beverage, and Food Products.
Industrial & Chemical: Fertilizer, Auto & Allied, Construction, Pharmaceuticals, Petroleum/Gas, and Chemicals.
Utilities: Electric, Power & Allied.
Buildings
Specifies requirements for Residential, Factory, and Commercial structures.
3. Key Indicators & Symbols
Checkmark (✓): Indicates that coverage for this specific risk is required for that category.
Cross (X): Indicates that coverage is generally not required or applicable for that category.
Red Cross: Specifically used under the Burglary column for Factory and Commercial buildings, highlighting a common exclusion or a specific area where guidance deviates.
4. General Note
At the bottom, a note clarifies that this chart is a minimum guidance tool.
Actual insurance decisions must be based on the specific nature, condition, and geographic location of the assets.

heading: Annexure FM: 9.22 Stock Report Monitoring Sheet
content:
This document is an Annexure FM: 9.22 Stock Report Monitoring Sheet, which tracks the financial and inventory position of a company over a 10-month period (from April 2013 to January 2014).
It is divided into several logical sections that detail assets, inventory breakdowns, and debt obligations.
1. Stock Position (Primary Summary)
This top section summarizes the total value of assets and the company's borrowing status.
Stocks & R/A: Tracks raw materials and receivables.
Total Borrowing: Shows the total debt the company has taken.
Margin: Expressed as a percentage (ranging from 29% to 37%), likely indicating the collateral margin required for loans.
Highlighting: The final column (Jan-14) is highlighted in yellow, indicating the most recent data point for the report.
2. Raw Cotton Breakdown
This section itemizes the types of raw cotton held in inventory:
Raw cotton local
Raw cotton imported
Raw cotton other/waste
Total Raw Cotton: The sum of the three categories above.
3. Processed Goods & Materials
This part lists the value of products at different stages of production and operational supplies:
Fibre, Yarn, and Fabric: Represents work-in-progress and finished textile goods.
Retail Outlet Stock: Inventory held at physical store locations.
Stores, Dyes, Chemicals Etc: Consumables used in the manufacturing process.
Total Stock: A calculated sum of all items in this section, which matches the Stocks figure in the very first section.
4. Borrowing Details (Bank Breakdown)
The bottom section provides a granular look at which financial institutions have provided loans to the company.
It lists various banks including:
ABL (Allied Bank Limited)
Al Baraka Bank Pakistan Limited
Askari Bank
Bank Alfalah - Islamic
BankIslami
Dubai Islamic Bank
MCB, NBP, NIB, and RBS
Total Borrowing: The bottom row aggregates these individual bank balances, which corresponds to the Total Borrowing figure at the top of the page.
